service.description: The receive service of the EdiX12 message type: keeps the bytes received on an authenticated connection (the REST endpoint's or the SFTP poll's remote) as they came, before anything is parsed, once per remote and content (store#ReceivedSystemMessage; a second delivery of the same bytes answers duplicateOfId and is not consumed again). Refuses a receipt with no remote (CONNECTION_REQUIRED).

The consume service of the EdiX12 message type: stores the receipt's interchanges, groups and documents (store#ReceivedInterchanges), validates each document, records each group's 997 when the profile sends them, applies each validated document through its profile's mapping service, each in a transaction of its own, then sends what this produced unless the connection batches. A receipt with a quarantined interchange is put in error, after the others were processed. Consuming a receipt again resumes from the statuses recorded.

Once per receipt: each interchange, quarantined when it cannot be trusted (no ISA, its form, version 00401, controls or trailer count, sender, receiver or usage other than its connection's), a duplicate when the same interchange was processed before, else accepted with its groups (rejected as a whole for a trailer, control, count, version or functional ID error, AK905) and documents (rejected for an ST/SE trailer, control or count error, AK502; else Stored).

A stored document on its grammar (segment order and occurrences, undefined segments; EdiHandler), the profile's element rules (required elements, types, lengths, its code subset) and the 850's totals (CTT01, CTT02, AMT*TT): Validated, or Rejected with the AK3/AK4 its 997 reports.

The 997 a received group is owed, once its documents are validated: a pending outbound document for the group. None for a 997 group (an acknowledgment is never acknowledged) or when the profile does not send 997s.

A validated document (or one in exception, retried) through its profile's mapping service, which applies it with Mantle's services and sets its status. The connection is locked, so two deliveries of one business document apply one after the other. A refusal throws its reason code.
A received document its mapping refused or failed on: Exception with the reason code, in a transaction of its own after the application rolled back.

Mapping service of a 997 sent: the body acknowledging the received group (AK1; an AK2 with AK3/AK4 and AK5 for each set unless the group is rejected as a whole; AK9 with the counts and the group's error code), from the validation recorded.

Mapping service of a 997 received: finds the group this side sent (AK1, by the connection's organization, partner and usage) and accepts or rejects each document sent in it (AK5, or AK9 for those it does not list), confirming or rejecting their SystemMessages. Refuses a 997 of a group or set not sent (ACK_UNMATCHED). Nothing is acknowledged back.

SECA on an order's status: an 855 for the decision on an order received in a purchase order (approved, cancelled or rejected), recorded in the business transaction as the order's next revision, and sent after the commit unless the connection batches.
SECA on a shipment shipped: an 856 for each EDI connection of its orders, recorded in the business transaction, sent after the commit.

SECA on an invoice's status: an 810 for a sales invoice of an order received in a purchase order when it reaches the profile's billing status, recorded in the business transaction, sent after the commit. Sending it is not a new accounting posting.

A pending document sent: its body from the profile's mapping service (in a transaction of its own; a refusal records the document Refused and sends nothing), checked on the set's grammar, in an interchange with ISA and GS control numbers allocated now under the connection scope's lock, kept with its outgoing SystemMessage (Produced) in this one transaction.

After a business transaction commits, and as the send_EdiPendingDocuments job: produces the pending documents (those given, else the oldest up to limit), each in a transaction of its own, then sends each produced document's SystemMessage and records it Sent. A document whose production failed stays Pending, one whose send failed stays Produced with its controls, for the next run; a rollback of the business transaction left no document to send.
A produced document whose SystemMessage was sent: Sent with the send date.

An operator's retry, keeping the document's identity: a received document in exception is applied again (after its crosswalk or master data was fixed), a refused one sent is produced and sent again, a produced one whose message is in error is sent again with the same bytes and controls. Refuses another status (NOT_RETRYABLE). Needs the EDI_ADMIN permission.

The documents sent that need attention: overdueList, per connection whose profile expects 997s, those sent (not 997s) longer ago than its ackOverdueMinutes (a day when not set) with no acknowledgment; and stuckList, those Pending or Produced longer than stuckMinutes (a crash after the commit, a failed send) or whose message is in error, and those Refused.

An operator's retry of a receipt left in error: an interchange quarantined while the connection was misconfigured (fixed since), or a document whose validation, 997 or application could not be recorded. It is consumed again from its kept bytes and records (consume#ReceivedSystemMessage with allowError): its quarantined interchanges are checked again (one now trusted replaces its quarantine, Superseded) and nothing done before is repeated. A resend of the same bytes is a duplicate receipt, so this is the way to recover it. Refuses a receipt not in error or received (NOT_RETRYABLE). Needs the EDI_ADMIN permission.
